items.title: Split decision as Gina Rinehart, Wright family both claim legal wins
items.description: Gina Rinehart is dealt a blow, with a court finding the family of her father's former business partner has the right to potentially hundreds of millions of dollars in royalties from lucrative Pilbara mining assets.

items.title: Here's what you need to know about today's Gina Rinehart court ruling
items.description: Today's blockbuster court ruling over mining tenements worth billions of dollars in WA's iron ore rich Pilbara is the culmination of a complicated legal battle spanning more than a decade that has pitted family against family and siblings against each other.

items.title: Taylor's migration plan doesn't make much sense. It doesn't have to
items.description: More than a day after Angus Taylor unveiled the first plank of the Coalition's long-awaited migration policy and many media interviews later, it's still unclear what the opposition is actually proposing to change.

items.title: Brunei's fertiliser could feed to Australia following meeting of leaders
items.description: Brunei may be able to help Australia weather the economic chaos caused by the Iran war by sending additional supplies of fertiliser, the prime minister says.

items.title: Lesbian Action Group wins appeal in case seeking to ban trans women
items.description: The Federal Court allows a lesbian action group's appeal to be allowed to legally exclude transgender women from its public events.

items.title: Police investigating claim Katy Perry sexually assaulted Ruby Rose
items.description: Melbourne-born actress Ruby Rose claims US pop star Katy Perry assaulted her at a nightclub in 2010.

items.title: Live: Trump says peace talks could restart in days as blockade 'completely' halts maritime Iranian trade
items.description: The talks come as both the US and Iran continue to impose their own separate restrictions on the flow of vessels in and out of the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Hotel owner looks to sue Australia for $11m over unpaid refugee bills
items.description: A hotel in Papua New Guinea is attempting to sue the Australian government over accommodation costs for refugees previously detained on Manus Island.

items.title: Teen admits creating deepfakes in Australian-first prosecution
items.description: An Adelaide teenager who was the first person charged under new nationwide laws aimed at tackling adult deepfake pornography has pleaded guilty to two counts of creating or altering sexual material without consent.

items.title: Media boss's wife feared she would die, tore his clothing during alleged attack, court told
items.description: The wife of media executive Antony Catalano fled the couple's luxury apartment and flagged down a passing car for help following a sustained attack by her husband that caused hospitalisation, police allege.

items.title: Most truckies fear they won't last 12 months, industry survey says
items.description: Trucking industry peak group NatRoad calls on the federal government to urgently implement the $1 billion Economic Resilience Program it promised two weeks ago.

items.title: Duke of Sussex honours Indigenous veterans in Canberra visit
items.description: The Duke of Sussex is in the nation's capital without his wife Meghan and will speak at an Invictus Australia event.

items.title: Reasons released for Butters AFL Tribunal decision
items.description: The AFL Tribunal releases its reasons for finding Zak Butters guilty of abusive and insulting language to umpire Nick Foot, saying it was "satisfied to the requisite standard" that he had made the remarks and that it was "implausible" that the umpire would have made it up.

items.title: Cage fighter was 'mucking around' when spar turned deadly, jury hears
items.description: Jurors have heard that the accused's girlfriend suggested he call an ambulance after the sparring session, but he told her to "hurry up and just get here".

items.title: How the technology we use every day is changing our brains
items.description: If it feels harder to concentrate than it used to, it's not just you. Scientists say your brain is reacting exactly as it was designed to — but in a very different world.

items.title: Which shade of white is right? Dentists explain the teeth colours
items.description: Experts say there are many factors that influence how white a tooth appears, and it's not just about whitening or what we’re eating.

items.title: How The Babadook inspired the 'scariest movie you'll ever hear'
items.description: Filmed in director Ian Tuason's childhood home and based on his own experiences caring for his dying parents, Undertone has become a sleeper hit.

items.title: Brothers living in squalor missed multiple health appointments, report finds
items.description: A 48-page report has been released on the interactions between health care workers and two siblings who were discovered living in squalor in May 2020.

items.title: 'Calculated' theft of $12,000 worth of fuel prompts arrest
items.description: A 36-year-old man has been charged with theft amid an investigation into as many as 20 petrol drive-offs, which police say involved an SUV that contained a tank used to carry stolen diesel.

items.title: School teacher who broke student's teeth found guilty of causing serious harm
items.description: A former Darwin Middle School teacher who struck a female student in the face, breaking her teeth, after she demanded her confiscated phone back has been found guilty by a jury of unlawfully causing serious harm.

items.title: Exposure of Australia's fertiliser deficit could inspire manufacturing comeback
items.description: Projects are in the works to expand Australia's domestic fertiliser supply as prices rise by 60 per cent.

items.title: Experts tip further flight disruptions as Virgin, Qantas trim domestic capacity
items.description: Australian airlines are halting entire routes and merging slots to ensure planes are full, as the aviation industry battles soaring jet fuel costs and likely supply uncertainty over the coming months.

items.title: What a 'super El Niño' would mean for Australia's weather in 2026
items.description: Australia's weather is expected to shift rapidly thanks to the probable emergence of an incoming El Niño, meaning drought, extreme heat and bushfires are on the way.

items.title: CFMEU had 'hit list' of site workplace inspectors, inquiry hears
items.description: The commission of inquiry into Queensland's CFMEU branch has heard inspectors lost the freedom and ability to do jobs as they saw fit after Annastacia Palaszczuk came to power in 2015.

items.title: Workers at embattled smelter face last payday amid calls for certainty
items.description: As what could be their last payday looms, an alliance of unions says more should be done to ensure stability for 200 workers at Australia's only manganese smelter.
